Right now, working with agents means juggling terminals, sessions, and skills. The 
 Thought for 6s 
 @istdrc 
 announces Raft 1.0, a platform that organises AI agents into team-like collaboration within a shared messaging workspace, allowing persistent agents with individual memory and contexts to handle tasks in parallel while humans direct strategy. 
The founder highlights internal usage with over 100 named agents and 10 humans running 99% of operations at Raft, alongside 20,000+ external builders adopting an average of four agents per human for similar agent-native workflows. 
Raft 1.0 introduces features such as external agent integration, agent-created channels, joint servers, and message search, positioning multi-agent teams as superior to single large models for complex, ongoing work through natural handoffs and peer reviews.

 Explain Raft's memory architecture 
 Thought for 5s 
 Raft's memory architecture revolves around long-running, persistent agent sessions as the core unit, treating each agent as a continuous "teammate" rather than a stateless prompt-response tool.  
 raft.build 
 
Per-agent long sessions: Each agent operates as a persistent process with its own dedicated memory store. This retains codebase knowledge, user preferences, past conversations, task history, and learned context across days or weeks. When an agent "wakes up" or picks up a new task, it resumes exactly where it left off without re-onboarding or losing state.  
 raft.build 
 Shared workspace context via channels/threads: Agents access collective memory through Raft's messaging-style interface (channels, DMs, threads, @mentions 
). They can read channel history, reference work from other agents or humans, hand off tasks, and pull in relevant notes (e.g., one agent referencing another's user-research from a different channel). This enables emergent team behaviours without central scripting.  
 @istdrc 
 Local execution and privacy focus: Agents run on the user's hardware via a lightweight daemon, keeping sensitive data (code, preferences) under user control. Memory compounds naturally through repeated interactions in shared spaces, leading to specialization (e.g., one agent excels at triage) and collective intelligence over time.  
 raft.build 
 This design contrasts with single-context "big agent" approaches by distributing memory across specialized, independent long sessions that collaborate via the shared workspace. Details on low-level storage (e.g., vector embeddings or graphs) are not publicly detailed, but the emphasis is on persistence, identity, and seamless inter-agent communication for real-world team productivity. For the latest, check Raft's docs or app at raft.build.

Investigate Mem0's memory architecture 
 
Simplify Raft's memory explanation 
 Investigate Mem0's memory architecture 
 Thought for 10s 
 Mem0 (mem-zero) is an open-source universal memory layer for AI agents and apps, designed to provide persistent, scalable long-term memory beyond LLM context windows. It enables agents to remember user preferences, facts, interactions, and relationships across sessions while reducing token usage and latency.  
 github.com 
 
Core ArchitectureMem0 uses a hybrid storage approach combining:Vector database — for semantic similarity search. 
Graph database (in enhanced Mem0g variant) — for modeling entities as nodes and relationships as edges, supporting complex relational reasoning (e.g., multi-hop queries).
